 any item on this agenda (other than writings legally exempt from public disclosure) will be
 made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk located at 6550 Miles
 Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
 p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

 Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including
 auxiliary aids or services, in order to participate in the public meeting may request such
 modification, accommodation, aid or service by contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in
 person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by telephone at (323) 584-6230.
 Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements
 to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

 PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC
 EQUIPMENT WHILE COUNCIL IS IN SESSION. Thank you.

PLEASE NOTE-The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA

  decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
 are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
 the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code, commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

 We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
 for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

 PUBLIC COMMENT

 For both open and closed sessions, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
 Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
 speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
 meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
 public hearing items.

 All comments or queries should be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
 member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
 Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
 on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
 direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

Public Hearing Opened: 7:39pm

Adrian Ortega- Spoke on the Item
 Public Hearing Closed: 7:42pm

  MOTION:  Councilmember Martiz stated that she would like to increase funds for
  kids and students. Proportion 42K towards the after school and other
  children’s programs and leave remainder for seniors for their
  programming. Councilmember Martiz and Mayor Martinez requested
  to bring back HUD guidelines for modification and review the
  eligibility for rehab programs. Councilmember Martiz motioned to
  approve the resolution approving the annual action plan with
  amendment stated for the public service funding as well as upcoming
  eligibility criteria changes to include multifamily homes for the rehab
  programs. Mayor Martinez seconded the motion. Councilmember
  Macias and Councilmember Flores voted no. The motion failed.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, and Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): Macias, and Flores

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  MOTION:  Councilmember Macias and Councilmember Flores stated that they
  do not want to remove any funding for senior programming and
  would rather proportionate general fund money to fund the children
  and youth programming. Mayor Martinez motioned support
  resolution but adds change eligibility to review and be able to expand
  funding for rental units. Councilmember Macias seconded the
  motion. Councilmember Martiz raised concerns about timeline and
  lack of flexibility. Director Morales stated that we do have flexibility,
  or timeline soon. However, due to nature of the change we would
  have to wait 30 days. Councilmember Martiz abstained.
  Councilmember Macias, Flores, and Mayor Martinez voted yes. The
  motion passed.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Macias, Flores, and Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): Martiz

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  Martinez voted yes on the motion. Councilmember Flores voted no

  DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Finance: No Report.

City Manager: Introduced new Assistant City Manager Stephany Santin

Assistant City Manager: Good evening, I am extremely excited to join the team. I have
already had a chance to work with several of the team members, and I look forward to the
opportunity to serve the city of Huntington Park.

City Attorney: No Report.

Police: No Report.

Parks and Recreation: Thank you to all who came out to Movie Night. There was a good
turnout, and there was an addition of telescopes in the back for the kids to check out the
stars. I Also want to thank everyone for the Keller groundbreaking that is coming up on
May 7th. The Avila Scholarship is still open and closes on Friday, May 1, 2026.

Community Development: No Report.

Public Works: Welcome Stephany to the team.

City Clerk: Thank you to the city council for filling the commission vacancies. Welcome to
Stephany Santin and look forward to collaborating with her.

Communication: Presentation on City’s Operating budget on May 7th @6pm. Inviting
public to attend. Continue providing information. We are getting good response on City
Wide beautification initiatives. Thank you for supporting children’s festivals. We will keep
looking for other options for the community pool. We are also looking for places to use for
the Council Meetings during the remodels. Art Walk Festival will be on May 17 th. We
invited our sister city Rosarito to attend. Deadline in on April 30th to submit. For the past
few years, we have been trying to unveil a utility box. This year for the 120 th anniversary
we are looking forward to a larger art walk event.
 WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Councilmember Martiz: Thank you everyone! Thank you for your hard work. Whenever
I hear that Huntington Parks Residence do not want to be associated with the Huntington
Park City Council she always thinks about the staff. How staff shows up every day.
Thank you for holding down the fort. Thank you for leading the change that we have
been working towards. Welcome to all the new staff.

Councilmember Macias: Thank you everyone! Have a good night.

Mayor Martinez: Thank you to staff for making sure we are here safe and well. Thank
you for volunteers who came out to community clean up. Thank you to colleagues and
city staff who came out and helped put that event together. The City’s Beautification
investment is staff that is going to go ahead and look at it. Coming up soon we will be
recognizing teachers of the year and top students from local schools at the Second
